To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of bulk density and water content on seedling root growth are complex and vary by species and soil.

(1) root length density response to compaction and moisture stress was best described using quadratic models for shortleaf and loblolly pine; and (2) shoot mass response to compaction, moisture stress, and LLWR differed by soil and species.

(1) root length density of seedlings grown on a compacted soil was affected by soil density, soil moisture, and the interaction between the two; (2) the least limiting water ranges (LLWR) of seedlings growing in a compacted soil were not always associated with root length density; and (3) root length density response surface models in combination with seasonal site water content data have potential for identifying compacted soil areas limiting tree growth.

soil water content and density interact to affect seedling root growth and shoot mass in different ways for different soils and species.

RLD and shoot mass response are complex and depend on soil properties, species, and water content.
